title: Every requirement, with the line that proves it.
lede: The verdict isn't a score: it comes from counting the requirements you meet. Open any row and check the count yourself.

verdict.label: The example's verdict
verdict.rule: Weak: a required item is missing, or two or more are only partly met. Partial: you meet the required items (one may be partly met) and fewer than two preferred ones. Strong: the same, with two or more preferred; a partly met one counts as half. Whatever a CV can't show stays out of the count.

requirements.hint: Open a row to see the note and the terms the posting names.

proof.note: Proves {{n}}, {{label}}: it names the tools and what he built with them. A line like this is worth more than “React” in a skills list.

readings.title: The other readings
readings.body: They look at your CV on its own and don't change the verdict. Three have a score; all of them show what they relied on.

ats.name: What an ATS reads
ats.reads: Which sections an applicant tracking system (ATS) can see, and whether any character in your PDF came out wrong.
ats.found: It sees Experience, Education and Languages. The text layer is clean.

experience.name: Experience & impact
experience.reads: Whether your bullets show results or only duties, with suggested rewrites that never invent numbers.
experience.found: You already put numbers on two results: 120 restaurants and 15 clients.

skills.name: Skills
skills.reads: Which of the skills the posting asks for you prove with a line of your CV, and which you only name.
skills.found: React, TypeScript and Node.js, each with its own line.

education.name: Education & certifications
education.reads: Whether your education counts for this role, and whether it comes across on your CV.
education.found: If you've finished any database courses, add them with the year.

tone.name: Tone & clarity
tone.reads: Tense, jargon, and how fast a reader gets to what matters.
tone.found: Every bullet starts with an action verb: they read quickly.

items.database: Name the database in the payments API bullet, and what you did with it.
items.aws: If you've deployed anything on AWS, add a line on what you deployed and how.
items.dashboard: Put a number on the order dashboard: how many orders it handles, or how much time it saves.
